To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
light scattering from 2-D arrays of Ag-nanoparticle separated by sub-10 nm gaps can be satisfactorilly interpreted by analytical formula derived from the dipole approximation.

the spectral evolution of light scattering from 2-D arrays of monodisperse Ag-nanoparticle can be satisfactorilly interpreted by analytical formula derived from the generic dipolar approximation and that the general formulism can be used to predict the Q factor of the array of metallic nano-structures.

light scattering spectra from 2D Ag-nanoparticle arrays with tunable interparticle spacing are interpreted by an analytical formula, which can be used as a design guideline to predict the Q factor and geometric characteristics of the array.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the light scattering from 2-D arrays of Ag nanoparticles separated by tunable gaps.
the fabrication of monodispensed metallic nano-particles separated by tunnable gaps and the study of their optical properties.
the light scattering properties of two dimensional arrays of monosized Ag-nanoparticle separated by tunable sub-10 nm gaps.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the plasmonic coupling is strongly dependent on the inter-nano-gap, and can be well understood by the analytical formulae.

the light scattering from the array can be satisfactorially interpreted by the analytical formulae derived in generic dipolar approximation and the Q factor of the plasmon resonance of the array can be predicted from the geometric characteristics of the array.

the plasmonic coupling between nanoparticles in a 2D array is determined by the interplay between the coupling strength, which is proportional to the gap size, and the dissipation of energy, which is proportional the gap size to the fourth power.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the light scattering spectra from an array of monodispersive metallic nanoparticles can be satisfactorally interpreted by the generic dipolar approximation, and the Q factor of the array can be estimated by the formulism derived from the generic dipolar formulae.
we have developed a new method to fabricate 2D arrays and to analyze their optical properties.

the light scattering spectrum of an array of Ag-nanoparticle is determined not only by the particle size and inter-particle distance but also by the shape, orientation, and arrangement of the array, which is a key issue to understand the optical properties of metallic nanoparticles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the plasmonic coupling between metallic nanoparticles can be controlled and tuned with high precision by the gap distance, which may find applications in designing plasmonic devices.
plasmonic coupling can be tuned by the interparticle distance, which is of fundamental importance in the design of plasmonic devices.
, the Q factor of a metallic nano-particle can be significantly improved by increasing the number of its nearest neighbors, while maintaining a constant gap size.
